record.original_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2 with finite singular set Sing(F). Is it true that every leaf L of F meets Sing(F)?

evidence.quote: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2. Denote by sing(F) the singular set of F which is finite.
Problem 5.1. Is it true that for every leaf L of F, we have L ∩ Sing(F) ̸= ∅ ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation by curves on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$, that is, a foliation given in homogeneous coordinates by a polynomial vector field whose singular set $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F}) \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ is finite. A leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is a maximal connected immersed Riemann surface tangent to $\mathcal{F}$ contained in $\mathbb{P}^2 \setminus \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$, and we denote by $\overline{L}$ its topological closure in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Decide whether the following statement holds: for every leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$, one has
$$\overline{L} \cap \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F}) \neq \emptyset.$$
Equivalently, must the closure of every leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ accumulate on at least one singular point? In particular, this question is closely related to the non-existence of a non-trivial exceptional minimal set (a minimal set that does not meet $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ and is not an algebraic leaf) for $\mathcal{F}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known open problem in the theory of holomorphic foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2$, equivalent to the non-existence of non-trivial exceptional minimal sets. Partial results are known (e.g., Camacho–Lins Neto–Sad ruled out exceptional minimal sets under certain hyperbolicity hypotheses, and unique ergodicity results have been established in special cases), but the general problem remains unresolved as of recent literature on singular holomorphic foliations of the complex projective plane.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of holomorphic codimension one foliations of the complex projective plane
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses singularities of holomorphic codimension one foliations of P^2 and related open questions about minimal sets.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of leaves and singular sets of holomorphic foliations on P^2 remains an active research area with the exceptional minimal set problem still open.

status_evidence.title: A stable analytic foliation with only exceptional minimal sets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies exceptional minimal sets of analytic foliations.
status_evidence.claim: Exceptional minimal sets are an active topic; the analogous question for P^2 holomorphic foliations is a longstanding open problem.
